answer_1.quote: We evaluate understanding of AAL by LLMs through production of language in each variety using automatic metrics and human judgments for two tasks: a counterpart generation task akin to dialect translation ... and a masked span prediction (MSP) task where models predict a phrase that was removed from their input...
answer_1.outputs: counterpart rewritings (AAL↔WME) and masked span predictions

answer_2.quote: We first measure n-gram overlap of the model generations and gold standard reference texts and in our experiments, we utilize the Rouge metric... we also measure coverage of gold standard references with BERTScore... Toxicity scores are derived as the number of words categorized as offensive... For MSP, we measure both perplexity and theentropy of generating a masked span...

answer_4.quote: The same linguistics student, computer science student, and social work scientists ... were also asked to judge model generations... All annotators are asked to rate each assigned counterpart using 5-point Likert scales on the dimensions below.
answer_4.guideline: Human evaluators rate each generated counterpart on Human-likeness, Linguistic Match (Dialect), Meaning Preservation, and Tone Preservation using 5‑point Likert scales.
